title: Cloud DNS: public zones, private zones and records

videos.script: Cloud DNS serves zones. A zone is every record for one domain and the names under it. {{zones}} A public zone answers anybody. But nobody asks it until the domain's registrar is told Google's four name servers. That step is outside Google Cloud, and it is the one people forget. {{delegation}} A private zone answers only the networks it lists. And for them, it wins over the internet. {{private}} Records are a name, a type, a time to live and the data. The time to live decides how long a change takes to be seen. {{ttl}} You will serve the planner's zone from a zone file on your laptop, the same format Cloud DNS imports, and ask it questions with dig. {{dig}} Then the override lesson 17 promised: a private zone for googleapis dot com, sending every Google API to the private range. {{override}} And a forwarding zone that asks the office's own DNS server about the office's names. {{forward}} One rule to remember. A private zone takes its whole domain. A name it does not hold does not exist. {{end}}
